```flow
Open the Genos Hub
Read what a skill does
Install it
Type / and run it
```

It is Monday and you need a status report. You could ask the AI in your own words, then correct it: shorter, include what is stuck, stop guessing. Someone has probably worked those instructions out already.

## Why it is hard

A good request takes several tries. You learn what to say about dates, what to leave out and what to check before anything is written. Doing that alone for every recurring job is slow, so most of us settle for the first answer.

## How Genos helps

A **skill** is a set of written steps with a name. You do not have to write your own: the **Genos Hub** holds every public skill, including ones from the Genos team.

Open one, read its steps and choose **Install**. It then shows up when you type `/` in the ask box. A teammate's shared skill works the same way, from **Team skills**. Installing is free on every plan and does not count against your skill limit.

A few general skills are installed for you from the start:

- **unread-summary**: what you missed, for example after days off
- **comments-waiting-on-me**: comments that wait for your answer
- **triage**: go through your Inbox and mentions
- **wrapup**: close out the day
- **weekly-review**: what got done, what slipped, what is next

Others in the Hub cover jobs such as meeting notes, status reports and writing a spec.

## What you get

- **A starting point instead of a blank box.** Steps are there to use or to learn from.
- **A list that stays yours.** Only your own and installed skills appear under `/`, and you can uninstall any of them.
- **You stay in charge.** Each skill says whether it is **Read only** or **Read and propose changes**. A proposed change waits for your approval.

Running a skill is asking Genos, so it uses your AI allowance. On Free, Genos follows the steps but changes nothing: it writes the text for you to copy. Making changes needs Core or above, and changing many items in one step needs Pro.

A public skill written by someone else, not the Genos team, is a stranger's text. Genos asks you to confirm it once for each version, and the only changes it can make are new tasks, notes and to-dos, each with your approval. Read the steps before you say yes.

## How to start

1. In the ask box (Cmd-K, or Ctrl-K), type `/` and run **unread-summary** or **weekly-review**.
2. Open **Settings → Genos → Skills**, then **Genos Hub**, and search for a job you repeat.
3. Install the skill, run it once and see what you would change.

If it is close but not quite your way, write your own and keep it.
